title: An Invitation With Too Much Ribbon
model_before: A transfer picture seems to justify a permanent pair.
model_after: The partner rule is a hypothesis to test against structure.

title: The Hall Beyond Every Window
model_before: The hall may be a flat collection of paired objects.
model_after: Ordinary NaCl is extended in three dimensions with labeled ionic species.

title: A Perfectly Balanced Wrong Picture
model_before: Correct equal totals appear to validate the pair structure.
model_after: Charge accounting and structural grouping need separate evidence.

title: The Balcony With an Ordinary Bench
model_before: Nearest neighbors might be owned by the selected center.
model_after: Local sixfold views overlap; access can be chosen without losing evidence.

title: Six Neighbors, One-to-One Composition
model_before: A local neighborhood count could be the formula ratio.
model_after: Six nearest neighbors and 1:1 bulk composition answer different questions.

title: The Archive of How They Arrived
model_before: Arrival transfer assigns a permanent partner and completes the explanation.
model_after: Electron counts, charge conservation and proton identity survive without partner memory.

title: Under the Floorboards
model_before: Attraction alone should collapse ions or end all motion.
model_after: Current many-particle interactions and electronic structure matter; schematic models have limits.

title: The Rehearsal That Went Dark
model_before: Patching a visible caption can repair every dependent representation.
model_after: Relationship records, entity counts and scope labels need coordinated repair.

title: Biscuits in the Unclassified Courtyard
model_before: Removing an invalid outline might make every grouping invalid.
model_after: A correction is bounded; discrete molecules and polyatomic groups remain meaningful.

title: Three Displays and Two Bad Drawers
model_before: One ionic/covalent drawer can classify an entire species.
model_after: Composition, charge, entity type and internal bonding are separate dimensions.

title: A Boundary Worth Keeping
model_before: A whole-ion tile might be one indivisible atom or a flat cross.
model_after: NH₄⁺ is a multiatom charged species with an eight-electron Lewis budget and tetrahedral model.

title: The Whole Ion Comes Along
model_before: Balancing charge is enough even if group contents change in printing.
model_after: Whole groups, charge totals and printed atom counts must all agree.

title: The Cargo That Lost Its Oxygen
model_before: Correct tiles guarantee a correct downstream formula and inventory.
model_after: Coefficients, group multipliers, internal subscripts and charges have distinct scopes.

title: The Smallest Fair Ledger
model_before: Any neutral count or any visible subscript reduction is acceptable.
model_after: The simplest neutral whole-ion ratio is required while supplied ion identities remain intact.

title: The Formula That Must Not Shrink
model_before: A common factor authorizes reducing every formula.
model_after: Molecular counts survive; an empirical ratio loses the molecular multiplier.

title: Two Cards That Refused the Shortcut
model_before: Familiar charges and visible even subscripts override supplied identity.
model_after: LiH and Na₂O₂ follow supplied intact ions, not unqualified shortcuts.

title: The Signmakers Disagree
model_before: A technically correct caption works regardless of scope or visibility.
model_after: Usable accurate communication keeps scope and access visible.

title: The Dance Without Pair Assignments
model_before: The repaired components may not work as one visitor-facing explanation.
model_after: The integrated exhibit preserves the distinctions without compulsory testing.

title: What the Old Chart Was Allowed to Keep
model_before: Correcting a model means discarding everything it once said.
model_after: A revision can retain valid counts, identities and uncertainty while removing the wrong claim.

title: The Useful Souvenir
model_before: Understanding requires carrying every detail unaided.
model_after: Portable questions and references support further learning without pretending to cover everything.
